page: Microsoft Azure D2as_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the DASv5 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an AMD EPYC 7763 processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz. The instance is configured with 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads, paired with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, though it is Premium Storage capable.

Performance benchmarks indicate a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The single-core CPU performance measured via stress-ng is strong, placing in the top 25%, while multi-core performance falls into the bottom 25%. Memory performance is a notable bottleneck, with Passmark memory scores and cached small-block memory bandwidth benchmarks ranking in the bottom 10%. Similarly, real-world application simulations show poor performance in database operations, static web serving throughput, and Redis SET operations, all scoring in the bottom 10%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D2as_v5 offers a low-cost entry point for workloads that require dedicated AMD EPYC CPU resources without the need for high memory bandwidth or local storage. Due to its weak multi-core scaling and poor database and web-serving throughput, this instance is best suited for lightweight, single-threaded tasks, basic development environments, or low-traffic background utility services rather than high-throughput web serving or database hosting.
